lessons.what: Deletes a folder, but only if it's empty.
lessons.when: Safely removing empty folders without risking anything inside.
lessons.tip: The 'safe mode' of deleting folders.

lessons.what: Tells you what kind of file something really is, no matter its name.
lessons.when: Someone sent 'photo.txt'. Is it really text? Or a JPEG in disguise?
lessons.tip: It reads the file's content, not just the extension.

lessons.man: display file or file system status
lessons.what: Shows full details of a file: size, permissions, owner and timestamps.
lessons.when: When was this file last changed? stat has the receipts.
lessons.tip: stat -c %s file prints just the size in bytes.

lessons.what: Converts a short or relative path into the full absolute path.
lessons.when: You need the full path to paste into a config or share with a friend.
lessons.tip: Great inside scripts to avoid path confusion.

lessons.man: strip directory and suffix from filenames
lessons.what: Takes a path and gives you just the file name.
lessons.when: In scripts, when you only care about 'song.mp3', not the long folder path.
lessons.tip: Add the extension as a 2nd argument to remove it.

quiz.q: rmdir only deletes folders that are...
file decides the type by looking at...
quiz.why: It inspects the data inside the file.

quiz.q: Which command shows a file's timestamps?

quiz.why: It resolves to the absolute path.

lessons.what: Arranges lines in order: alphabetical, numeric or reverse.
lessons.when: Turning a messy list of names or marks into a neat ranked list.
lessons.tip: -n numeric, -r reverse, -h human sizes like 2K 1G.

lessons.what: Removes repeated lines that sit next to each other.
lessons.when: Your attendance list has duplicate names. Clean it up.
lessons.tip: Always sort first: uniq only catches neighbours.

lessons.man: remove sections from each line of files
lessons.what: Picks out specific columns or characters from each line.
lessons.when: You only want the 'name' column from a big CSV.
lessons.tip: -d = separator, -f = which field (column).

lessons.what: Replaces or deletes characters as text flows through.
lessons.when: Converting text to uppercase, or removing all the digits.
lessons.tip: -d deletes the characters you list.

lessons.what: Adds line numbers to a file's lines.
lessons.when: Sharing code with a friend: 'check line 12' is easier with numbers.
lessons.tip: By default, nl skips numbering empty lines.

quiz.q: Which flag makes sort compare numbers?

quiz.why: Sorting puts duplicates next to each other.
Each lowercase letter maps to uppercase.

lessons.man: concatenate and print files in reverse
lessons.what: Prints a file upside down: last line first.
lessons.when: Reading a diary or log newest-first. (It's cat spelled backwards!)
lessons.tip: cat -> tac. Linux has jokes too.

lessons.what: Reverses the characters in each line.
lessons.when: Checking palindromes, or grabbing the last part of a line easily.
lessons.tip: rev | cut | rev is a classic trick for 'last column'.

lessons.what: Joins files side by side, line by line.
lessons.when: You have names in one file and marks in another. Stitch them together.
lessons.tip: -d sets the separator (default is a tab).

lessons.man: read from standard input and write to standard output and files
lessons.what: Shows output on screen AND saves it to a file at the same time.
lessons.when: You want to watch the results and keep a copy too.
lessons.tip: -a appends instead of overwriting. Named after a T-pipe.

lessons.what: Shows exactly what changed between two files.
lessons.when: Your code worked yesterday and not today. What did you change?
lessons.tip: diff -u gives the format used by Git.

quiz.why: It's cat in reverse line order.
rev reverses characters on each line.
Line 1 with line 1, line 2 with line 2...

lessons.what: Searches for a word inside files and prints matching lines.
lessons.when: Which of your 50 note files mentions 'exam date'?
lessons.tip: -i ignore case, -r all files in folder, -n line numbers.

lessons.man: search for files in a directory hierarchy
lessons.what: Finds files by name, type, size or age.
lessons.when: You saved an assignment somewhere. Somewhere. Find it.
lessons.tip: -mtime -1 = modified in the last 24 hours.

lessons.man: compare two files byte by byte
lessons.what: Checks if two files are exactly identical.
lessons.when: Are these two downloaded files the same, or is one corrupted?
lessons.tip: Works on any file, not just text.

lessons.man: compare two sorted files line by line
lessons.what: Shows lines unique to file 1, unique to file 2, and common to both.
lessons.when: Who's in both the football team and the chess club?
lessons.tip: Files must be sorted. -12 shows only common lines.

lessons.what: Formats messy text into neat, aligned columns.
lessons.when: Making a CSV readable in the terminal, like a quick table.
lessons.tip: -t makes a table, -s sets the separator.

quiz.why: It matches file names ending in .pdf.

quiz.q: comm needs its input files to be...

lessons.what: Bundles many files into one archive (and can compress it).
lessons.when: Submitting a whole project folder as a single file.
lessons.tip: c create, x extract, t list, z gzip, f file name.

lessons.what: Compresses a file to make it smaller (adds .gz).
lessons.when: A huge text file is eating your disk. Shrink it.
lessons.tip: gzip replaces the original. -k keeps it.

lessons.what: Decompresses a .gz file back to normal.
lessons.when: You downloaded data.csv.gz and need the actual CSV.
lessons.tip: Same as gzip -d.

lessons.what: Creates a .zip archive, the format every OS understands.
lessons.when: Sending files to a friend who uses Windows.
lessons.tip: -r includes everything inside folders.

lessons.man: list, test and extract compressed files in a ZIP archive
lessons.what: Extracts files from a .zip archive.
lessons.when: Your lecturer sent 'lab_files.zip'. Open it up.
lessons.tip: -l lists contents first, -d picks where to extract.

quiz.q: In tar -czf, what does c mean?
quiz.why: c = create a new archive (z does compression).
gzip replaces the original unless you use -k.
